subject: Elevated attention: FastRetail platform health & coordination
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fastretail.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Lo <ethan.lo@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 09:30:12 -0700
Subject: Spike in errors and timeouts on /generate during morning peak

Team —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 500-level errors and timeouts hitting the /generate endpoint around 09:12 PT. Error rate peaked at ~32% and our checkout traffic is getting throttled. This is causing failed personalization writes and customer-facing timeouts.

What we observed:
- ~30% error rate on /generate between 09:12 and 09:26 PT
- Increased tail latency (p99 > 2.4s) on several routes
- Throughput to your endpoint dropped ~40% during the same window

Attached is a brief sample of errors and one stack trace. Please advise immediate next steps and whether you have a mitigation timeline. We need a short customer-facing note we can share with our leadership and ops teams.

Attachment: fastretail-error-sample.log (text)

— Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Platform Reliability
FastRetail
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 09:45:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in errors and timeouts on /generate during morning peak

Samira —

Thanks for the flag and the sample log. We're elevating this to an immediate incident standup. I’ve looped in our on-call infra and product leads (cc’d).

Immediate actions we are taking
- Standup in 10 minutes to gather telemetry and isolate the degradation vector
- Temporarily increase burst capacity for your tenant to reduce queueing
- Start live tailing of the affected nodes and collect KV cache stats

Can you confirm whether you see any correlated change in request profile (longer prompts or higher concurrency from clients) since 09:00? Also please share any customer-facing SLAs we should be mindful of.

I will send regular status updates to you and your ops team every 30 minutes until resolved. Apologies for the disruption — we prioritize restoring healthy throughput and low tail latency.

Attachment: screenshot-error-500.png (png)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: Spike in errors — coordination and quick triage plan

Folks —

Looping you into FastRetail’s alert (below). Short plan for the next 90 minutes:
1) Incident bridge at 10:00 PT — dial-in and run through roles (SRE, Runtime, Routing, CS)
2) Apply a targeted capacity bump for FR tenancy and pin to a stable model shard
3) Collect per-node KV cache hit rates and per-model latency distributions (p50/p95/p99)
4) If autoscaler loop is implicated, temporarily disable aggressive downscaling for the affected pool

Owner assignments:
- David: lead triage on serving runtime and confirm whether kernel degradation or memory pressure is present
- Laura: CS lead and external comms owner (customer updates and leadership note)
- Marissa: bridge commander / exec liaison
- Monica: telemetry sweep and APM correlation (traces/Spans)

Please join the bridge: meet.redwood.com/incidents/fastretail-0702 (we’ll open at 10:00).

- Autoscaler activity: 3 scale-down events between 09:00–09:18 that correlate with rising queue length
- Request profile: 12% of requests are >350 tokens (higher than historical 4%) — likely larger prompts from FastRetail A/B test

External comms draft (for Samira):
- Acknowledgement of impact
- Summary of immediate mitigations (capacity bump, autoscaler hold)
- Estimated mitigation ETA: 60–90 minutes, contingent on trace validation

I’ll prepare a short note for our CEO/COO in case they want to escalate a briefing. Link to the telemetry snapshot: https://drive.google.com/telemetry/fastretail/0702

From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 10:40:08 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Spike in errors — coordination and quick triage plan

Team —

Post-bridge technical update:
- Root cause candidate: autoscaler downscaling startled the S-42 worker pool during a spike in long-prompt requests. When workers rejoined, KV caches were cold, causing burst of long-tail model compute and request queueing.
- Actions taken:
  * Temporarily held scale-down for S-42 pool and applied emergency capacity +2 nodes to that pool
  * Pre-warmed KV cache snapshot to the new nodes (replayed recent prefixes)
  * Rolled a small patch to the request router to favor warmed shards for FR tenancy while we validate
- Observed effect: error rate dropped from 32% to ~6% within 12 minutes after capacity bump; p99 latency decreased from 2.4s to 0.9s

Next steps:
- Keep the scale-down hold for 2 hours and monitor for regression
- Create post-incident RCA if metrics hold for 24 hours

Attachment: fix_runbook.md (md)

— David
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fastretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Status update — FastRetail incident (summary & next steps)

Samira —

Thank you again for raising this. Short summary of current state and what we did: 

What happened (short):
- Morning traffic included an unexpected shift to longer prompts from a FastRetail experiment which led to worker pool S-42 being briefly scaled down and then overwhelmed when longer compute began. Cold KV caches amplified the latency and error surface.

What we did: 
- Emergency +2 node capacity for S-42, held scale-down for 2 hours
- Pre-warmed KV caches on the new nodes and adjusted router to prefer warmed shards for your tenancy
- Continuous monitoring in place; CS-led customer cadence established

Current status:
- Errors reduced to <5% and p99 latency back below 1s across the affected routes
- We’ll keep the safeguards in place for 2 hours and then follow a controlled rollback if metrics remain stable

Customer-facing note we recommend sending to your stakeholders (feel free to adapt):
> We experienced elevated errors and latency this morning due to a surge of long-form requests tied to an A/B test. Redwood implemented emergency capacity, pre-warmed model caches, and routing changes; the issue is now mitigated and we are monitoring for 24 hours. Estimated full confidence in rollback: 48 hours and a post-incident report within 5 business days.

We will share the RCA and a proposed change to autoscaler thresholds (to avoid aggressive downscaling on spiky long-request profiles). I’ll stay on this and am available if your leadership wants a call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
